subject: System Design
title: Global Consistency with CRDTs
description: A micro-lesson that makes Global Consistency with CRDTs usable.

hook.text: Two users edit the same document in different countries simultaneously. Who wins?

buildup.text: CRDTs — Conflict-free Replicated Data Types — are data structures that merge without conflicts.

discovery.text: A CRDT counter at two nodes can be incremented independently. The merged result is always correct.

twist.text: CRDTs only work for specific operations. Not all data models can be made conflict-free.

climax.text: CRDTs enable truly distributed, conflict-free collaboration — the secret behind tools like Figma.

punchline.text: Data structures that merge without conflicts.

quiz.question: What are CRDTs?
options: Data structures that merge without conflicts across replicas
